newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas extends losses ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas extends losses ahead of holiday.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices softened further Tuesday, but business was sparse as most traders had already locked in their deals through the holiday, sources said.
Louisiana Gulf prices notionally fell another five to 10 cents to the $3.80s to about $3.90, down about 60 cents from week-ago levels but even with most December indices.
Sources attributed the weaker swing cash market to milder weather, softness in the expiring futures market and an expected drop in demand over the holiday.
NYMEX Jan Henry Hub futures was trading at $4.10 at 1226 EST, down 9.2 cents from Monday's settlement but significantly lower than the $4.60 contract high achieved one week ago.
In the East, temperatures are expected to dip to about five to nine degrees below normal Wednesday but then moderate to near-normal by Thursday.
As a result, prices at the New York city-gate lost another 10 cents to the $4.10-4.15 range, but most gas flows had already been scheduled on Monday.
Midcontinent prices slipped into the high $3.50s to mid-$3.60s, down about five cents, with Northern at Demarcation quoted around $3.80.
In west Texas, Permian gas prices plummeted to about $3.50 in very light trade, down about 30 cents from Monday.

Lending support to the southern California border market was the rally in the domestic Canadian market to above $4 per gigajoule at the AECO storage hub as cold weather struck the province. Prices were notionally talked in the low-$3.90s, but no deals could be confirmed done.
